captions.instagram:
How does the circulatory system work?

Five litres of blood go round your body about once a minute, through a network that reaches almost every cell. Follow one red blood cell to the lungs and back, squeeze an arteriole and watch the flow collapse, see what leaks out of a capillary, and plug a cut.

→ Your blood runs through a network that reaches almost every cell you have.
→ Arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins bring it back, and capillaries join them.
→ Blood makes two loops: right heart to the lungs, then left heart out to the body.
→ Run, and the heart pumps four times more, and most of it floods your muscles.
→ From 120 over 80 in the aorta, pressure falls to almost nothing by the time blood gets home.

youtubeLong.title: How does the circulatory system work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Five litres of blood go round your body about once a minute, through a network that reaches almost every cell. Follow one red blood cell to the lungs and back, squeeze an arteriole and watch the flow collapse, see what leaks out of a capillary, and plug a cut.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/circulationclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/circulationclear

In this video:
• A network in every part of you. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins bring it back, and about 10 billion capillaries join them in every organ.
• Two loops, one lap a minute. Right heart to the lungs and back, then left heart to the body and back: a double circulation.
• From 120 over 80 to almost nothing. Pressure falls from about 120/80 in the aorta to about 35 then 15 mmHg across the capillaries.
• Swap at the capillaries. Oxygen and glucose diffuse out, carbon dioxide diffuses in.
• What blood is. About 55% plasma and 40–45% red cells, with white cells and platelets in a thin layer.
• Keeping it healthy. High blood pressure affects about 1 in 4 adults in India and usually has no symptoms.
